history: Ms. L is a 43-year-old postal carrier who has been feeling worn out for several months. She says climbing two flights of stairs now leaves her unusually winded and she needs to pause to catch her breath. She mentions her periods have been heavier over the last year and she often skips meat because of her vegetarian diet. She denies chest pain, cough, fevers, or recent infections. She has migraines treated with ibuprofen as needed; her mother had uterine fibroids. She does not smoke and drinks wine socially.

imaging_results.Chest X-ray: Clear lungs with normal cardiac silhouette.

case_explanation: Fatigue with pallor and low hemoglobin suggests iron deficiency anemia.
full_explanation: Fatigue and dyspnea with pallor suggests anemia. CBC and ferritin confirm iron deficiency. Imaging is normal. In future patients, evaluate bleeding risk and iron studies early.

history: A 45-year-old office manager says she has been moving in slow motion for about six months. She feels cold when others are comfortable, has been constipated, and notices her skin is drier than usual. She has gained weight despite no major diet changes and says her hair feels coarse. She has hyperlipidemia and takes a statin; her sister has Hashimoto thyroiditis. No fevers, night sweats, or recent travel.
case_explanation: Fatigue with weight gain and high TSH suggests hypothyroidism.
full_explanation: Symptoms and exam point to hypothyroidism. TSH and free T4 confirm. Ultrasound supports diffuse thyroid changes. In future cases, screen thyroid function with fatigue plus weight gain.

history: A 52-year-old long-haul truck driver complains of feeling tired all day even after what he thinks is a full night of sleep. His partner has noticed loud snoring and pauses in breathing, and he often wakes with a headache and a dry mouth. He admits he has gained weight and drinks several cups of coffee just to stay alert on the road. He has hypertension treated with amlodipine. He denies chest pain or syncope.
case_explanation: Snoring with daytime somnolence suggests obstructive sleep apnea.
full_explanation: Daytime sleepiness with snoring suggests OSA. Exam shows crowded airway. Sleep study confirms apneas. In future patients, screen for sleep apnea when fatigue is prominent.

history: A 29-year-old engineer reports two weeks of low energy, low-grade fevers, and body aches. He says it started a few days after a camping trip and he has had mild headaches and a reduced appetite since then. He has no cough, shortness of breath, or urinary symptoms and is still going to work, but feels run down. He has seasonal allergies but no chronic illnesses. He does not smoke and drinks beer on weekends.
case_explanation: Fatigue with low-grade fever and normal imaging suggests viral illness.
full_explanation: Inflammatory symptoms without focal findings suggest viral illness. Basic labs show inflammation. Imaging is normal. In future patients, use exposure history and supportive care.

history: A 52-year-old librarian presents with a week of fever and a productive cough that makes her rattle when she breathes. She feels short of breath when climbing stairs and has right-sided chest discomfort with deep breaths. She smokes about half a pack per day and uses an albuterol inhaler for mild COPD. She has no recent travel and no known sick contacts.
case_explanation: Fever with focal crackles and CXR opacity suggests pneumonia.
full_explanation: Fever with focal lung findings suggests pneumonia. CBC shows leukocytosis. Chest X-ray confirms opacity. In future cases, localize findings and image promptly.

history: A 34-year-old woman reports several days of burning urination followed by fevers, chills, and now right-sided flank pain. She says the pain is constant and she feels nauseated and weak. She has had UTIs before but no kidney stones. She is sexually active, not pregnant, and takes no daily medications. No cough or sore throat.
case_explanation: Fever with flank pain and positive UA suggests pyelonephritis.
full_explanation: Fever and flank pain with positive UA indicates pyelonephritis. CVA tenderness supports upper tract infection. Imaging excludes obstruction. In future cases, treat promptly and assess severity.

history: A 19-year-old college student says her throat has been very sore for three days and swallowing is painful. She has fevers, feels exhausted, and has been eating less because it hurts to swallow. Several classmates are sick. She denies cough. She has no significant past medical history and takes an oral contraceptive.

exam_results.HEENT exam: Tonsillar exudates and tender anterior cervical nodes.

case_explanation: Exudative pharyngitis with fever suggests strep.
full_explanation: Fever with exudates and tender nodes suggests strep pharyngitis. Labs show inflammation. Imaging is normal. In future cases, use Centor criteria to guide testing.

history: A 60-year-old man with long-standing diabetes is brought in by family for fever and confusion over two days. They note he has been drinking lots of water and urinating frequently and seemed out of it this morning. He ran out of insulin two days ago and has not checked his glucose. He also has hypertension and hyperlipidemia. He denies cough, dysuria, or abdominal pain.
case_explanation: Fever with severe hyperglycemia and anion gap suggests DKA.
full_explanation: Fever and confusion with hyperglycemia suggests DKA. Exam shows dehydration. BMP confirms metabolic derangement. Imaging rules out infection. In future patients, check glucose and ketones early.

history: A 38-year-old fitness instructor says she has been losing weight without trying and feels on edge most days. She notices heat intolerance, frequent bowel movements, and intermittent palpitations that make her anxious. She drinks two energy drinks a day and struggles to sleep. Her mother has Graves disease. No fevers or night sweats.
case_explanation: Weight loss with suppressed TSH suggests hyperthyroidism.
full_explanation: Weight loss with palpitations and heat intolerance suggests hyperthyroidism. Labs confirm. Ultrasound shows diffuse changes. In future cases, check thyroid labs early.

history: A 58-year-old man reports a 6-month history of weight loss and intermittent blood in his stool. He feels more tired than usual and gets winded with activity. He denies abdominal pain but notes his stools can be thinner than before. He smokes one pack per day and eats a low-fiber diet. He has never had a colonoscopy.

lab_results.Iron studies: Low ferritin and low iron saturation.

imaging_results.Colonoscopy: Friable mass in the sigmoid colon.

case_explanation: Weight loss with anemia and colon mass suggests colon cancer.
full_explanation: Weight loss with hematochezia suggests malignancy. Colonoscopy shows a mass. In future cases, prioritize colonoscopy for red-flag symptoms.

history: A 46-year-old man has had a chronic cough for two months, with night sweats and unintentional weight loss. He recently stayed in a crowded shelter and has had limited access to healthcare. He drinks alcohol occasionally and does not use drugs. No recent travel outside the country.
case_explanation: Weight loss with night sweats and cavitary lesions suggests TB.
full_explanation: Chronic cough and night sweats suggest TB. Imaging shows cavitary lesions. In future cases, assess exposure risk and isolate early.

history: A 31-year-old woman reports months of chronic diarrhea, bloating, and weight loss. She says symptoms are worse after eating bread or pasta and she feels tired most afternoons. Her primary care doctor recently told her she was iron deficient. She denies fevers or blood in stool. Her aunt has celiac disease.
case_explanation: Weight loss with chronic diarrhea suggests celiac disease.
full_explanation: Chronic diarrhea and weight loss suggest malabsorption. Endoscopy shows duodenal changes. In future cases, consider celiac disease with GI symptoms and anemia.

history: A 45-year-old office manager says she has been gaining weight despite no change in diet. She feels fatigued, constipated, and cold much of the time, and her skin has become dry and coarse. She has hyperlipidemia and takes atorvastatin. Her sister has autoimmune thyroid disease. No recent illness or medication changes.
case_explanation: Weight gain with high TSH indicates hypothyroidism.
full_explanation: Weight gain with cold intolerance suggests hypothyroidism. Labs confirm. In future patients, screen thyroid function.

history: A 37-year-old woman reports central weight gain, easy bruising, and proximal muscle weakness over the past year. She has noticed new purple stretch marks on her abdomen and feels her face looks rounder in photos. She has hypertension treated with a thiazide and denies exogenous steroid use.
case_explanation: Central weight gain with striae suggests Cushing syndrome.
full_explanation: Central weight gain with striae and weakness suggests Cushing syndrome. Exam shows moon facies. In future cases, assess steroid exposure and endocrine testing.

history: A 66-year-old man with hypertension reports rapid weight gain over several weeks with leg swelling and shortness of breath on exertion. He now sleeps on two pillows and feels more tired than usual. He had a remote myocardial infarction and takes lisinopril and metoprolol. No fever or cough.
case_explanation: Weight gain with edema and elevated BNP suggests heart failure.
full_explanation: Volume overload signs with elevated BNP indicate heart failure. In future cases, assess volume status and cardiac function.

history: A 29-year-old woman presents with puffiness around her eyes and ankle swelling for two weeks. She also notices foamy urine and a few pounds of weight gain. She had a viral upper respiratory illness three weeks ago. No fevers or flank pain. No known kidney disease.
case_explanation: Edema with proteinuria suggests nephrotic syndrome.
full_explanation: Edema and heavy proteinuria indicate nephrotic syndrome. Imaging is often normal. In future cases, quantify proteinuria and evaluate causes.

history: A 67-year-old man on a thiazide diuretic reports diffuse weakness and muscle cramps over several days. He has no focal neurologic deficits and denies chest pain or shortness of breath. He has diabetes controlled with metformin and notes poor appetite since a recent GI illness.
case_explanation: Low potassium with weakness indicates hypokalemia.
full_explanation: Diffuse weakness after diuretic use suggests hypokalemia. BMP confirms. Imaging is normal. In future cases, check electrolytes early.

history: A 70-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation reports sudden onset weakness on her right side and slurred speech that began one hour ago. She was well earlier in the day and has no headache or loss of consciousness. She takes apixaban inconsistently due to cost.

imaging_results.MRI Brain: Acute infarct in left MCA territory.

case_explanation: Focal deficits with infarct indicate ischemic stroke.
full_explanation: Sudden focal weakness suggests stroke. Imaging confirms infarct. In future cases, treat as time-sensitive emergency.

history: A 52-year-old man with diabetes developed shakiness, sweating, and weakness after taking his usual insulin but skipping lunch. He feels anxious and lightheaded and says it improved slightly after drinking juice. He has had similar episodes when he skips meals.
case_explanation: Low glucose with weakness indicates hypoglycemia.
full_explanation: Autonomic symptoms with low glucose indicate hypoglycemia. In future cases, check bedside glucose early.

history: A 33-year-old woman reports fluctuating weakness with drooping of her eyelids and difficulty chewing late in the day. Symptoms worsen with prolonged activity and improve with rest. She denies sensory loss or bowel/bladder changes. She has no significant past medical history.
case_explanation: Fatigable weakness with ptosis suggests myasthenia gravis.
full_explanation: Fatigable weakness with ocular findings suggests myasthenia gravis. Imaging can show thymic pathology. In future cases, look for diurnal variation and ocular symptoms.

history: A 36-year-old woman says she has felt progressively fatigued for months and gets lightheaded when she stands up quickly. She has been craving salty foods and noticed her skin looks darker, especially in skin creases and around old scars. She has lost weight without trying and feels weaker when she climbs stairs. She took a short prednisone course for bronchitis about six months ago. She has no diabetes or thyroid disease; her father has vitiligo. She is not on daily medications.

exam_results.Skin exam: Diffuse hyperpigmentation, especially in palmar creases.

case_explanation: Fatigue with orthostatic hypotension, hyperpigmentation, and low cortisol suggests adrenal insufficiency.
full_explanation: Systemic symptoms plus hyperpigmentation and electrolyte abnormalities point to primary adrenal insufficiency. Low cortisol with elevated ACTH confirms primary disease. In future cases, check cortisol and ACTH when fatigue pairs with orthostasis and hyperpigmentation.

history: A 41-year-old man reports about ten days of fevers, chills, and feeling generally unwell. He notes pleuritic chest pain and admits to poor dental care and injection drug use. He has hepatitis C and has not seen a doctor in years. He denies recent travel or known sick contacts.

exam_results.Cardiac auscultation: New holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border.

case_explanation: Fever with new murmur, peripheral stigmata, and positive cultures suggests endocarditis.
full_explanation: Fever in a person who injects drugs with a new murmur and tender finger nodules suggests endocarditis. Blood cultures and echo confirm vegetations. In future cases, obtain multiple blood cultures before antibiotics.

history: A 65-year-old man reports progressive weight loss and painless jaundice over two months. He has dark urine, pale stools, and diffuse itching that keeps him up at night. He has a long smoking history and decreased appetite. He has type 2 diabetes and takes metformin. No abdominal pain.

imaging_results.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: Mass in the head of the pancreas with biliary ductal dilation.

case_explanation: Weight loss with painless jaundice and a pancreatic head mass suggests pancreatic cancer.
full_explanation: Painless obstructive jaundice with weight loss and Courvoisier sign suggests pancreatic malignancy. Cholestatic labs and CT confirm a pancreatic head mass. In future cases, pursue cross-sectional imaging for painless jaundice.

history: A 58-year-old man with long-standing alcohol use reports increasing abdominal girth, early satiety, and leg swelling over six weeks. He bruises easily and feels more fatigued than usual. He has a history of hepatitis C and has not seen a doctor in years. No hematemesis or melena.
case_explanation: Rapid weight gain with ascites, stigmata of liver disease, and low albumin suggests cirrhosis.
full_explanation: Abdominal distension, shifting dullness, and chronic liver stigmata point to cirrhosis with ascites. Labs show synthetic dysfunction and ultrasound confirms nodular liver with fluid. In future cases, evaluate ascites with ultrasound and liver function tests.

history: A 49-year-old man presents with rapidly progressive ascending weakness and tingling four days after a diarrheal illness. He is struggling to climb stairs and feels short of breath when lying flat. He had a similar but milder episode years ago after influenza. No bowel or bladder incontinence.

exam_results.Neuro strength exam: Symmetric 3/5 weakness in legs greater than arms.

lab_results.CSF analysis: Elevated protein with normal cell count.

case_explanation: Ascending weakness with areflexia and albuminocytologic dissociation suggests GBS.
full_explanation: Rapidly progressive ascending weakness after infection with areflexia suggests GBS. CSF shows elevated protein with normal cells and MRI rules out compression. In future cases, monitor respiratory status early.

history: A 28-year-old daycare worker says she has had a dry cough for about a week with low-grade fevers and a dull headache. Several children at her daycare had similar symptoms. She feels a little more tired than usual but denies chest pain or shortness of breath. She has no chronic illnesses and takes no daily medications.
case_explanation: Dry cough with interstitial infiltrates suggests atypical pneumonia.
full_explanation: Subacute dry cough with low-grade fever and interstitial CXR pattern suggests atypical pneumonia. Mild inflammatory markers support infection. In future cases, consider atypical pathogens when symptoms are mild but persistent.

history: A 35-year-old man reports a nagging cough that wakes him at night and occasional wheezing, especially when he exercises or goes out in cold air. He has seasonal allergies and eczema and says his chest sometimes feels tight. He has no fever or sputum production and has never smoked.
case_explanation: Nocturnal cough with wheezing and atopy suggests asthma.
full_explanation: Episodic cough and wheeze with atopy and hyperinflation suggest asthma. Eosinophilia supports allergic inflammation. In future cases, ask about triggers and consider spirometry.

history: A 62-year-old man has a dry, persistent cough for six months and a hoarse voice, especially in the mornings. He says it worsens when he lies down after dinner and he often tastes acid in his throat. He has a history of heartburn but no lung disease. He takes no ACE inhibitors.
case_explanation: Chronic cough with heartburn and hoarseness suggests reflux-related cough.
full_explanation: Chronic cough without pulmonary findings plus hoarseness and heartburn suggests reflux. Normal CXR helps exclude lung disease. In future cases, screen for reflux symptoms when cough is chronic.

history: A 57-year-old woman developed a constant dry cough about three weeks after starting a new blood pressure medication. She denies fever, sputum, or chest pain and says the cough is worse at night. She has hypertension and osteoarthritis and recently started lisinopril.
case_explanation: Dry cough after ACE inhibitor initiation suggests medication side effect.
full_explanation: Temporal relationship to ACE inhibitor with normal exam and imaging suggests ACE inhibitor cough. In future cases, review medication changes when cough is new.

history: A 47-year-old man reports a chronic cough with night sweats and weight loss for two months. He says the cough is worse at night and sometimes brings up blood-tinged sputum. He recently moved in with relatives after a period of housing instability. No recent travel outside the country.
case_explanation: Chronic cough with night sweats and apical cavities suggests TB.
full_explanation: Constitutional symptoms with apical cavitation in a high-risk patient suggests TB. In future cases, isolate early and obtain sputum testing.

history: A 17-year-old boy says his throat has been very sore for five days and he feels extremely fatigued. He notes fevers, poor appetite, and a sense of abdominal fullness. He had a roommate with a similar illness. He has no chronic medical problems and does not smoke.

exam_results.HEENT exam: Tonsillar exudates and posterior cervical lymphadenopathy.

imaging_results.Neck Ultrasound: Enlarged cervical lymph nodes without abscess.

case_explanation: Exudative pharyngitis with posterior nodes and atypical lymphocytes suggests mono.
full_explanation: Posterior cervical nodes, splenomegaly, and atypical lymphocytosis suggest EBV mononucleosis. Heterophile antibody confirms. In future cases, avoid contact sports with splenomegaly.

history: Ms. J is a 23-year-old barista who comes in with a sudden sore throat and fever for two days. She says swallowing feels like razor blades and she stayed home from her shift because she feels wiped out. She denies cough or runny nose and has not traveled recently. She has no chronic medical problems, takes no daily medications, and her roommate had a similar illness last week. She does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially.

exam_results.HEENT exam: Tonsillar exudates with tender anterior cervical nodes.

case_explanation: Fever, exudates, and positive rapid test indicate strep pharyngitis.
full_explanation: Classic Centor features with positive rapid test confirm strep pharyngitis. In future cases, test and treat to prevent complications.

history: Mr. P is a 44-year-old high school teacher who presents with severe throat pain that started yesterday and has rapidly worsened. He says his voice sounds muffled, he is drooling because it hurts to swallow, and even sips of water are painful. He has high fevers and feels very ill. He had a sore throat last week but did not seek care. He takes no daily medications, does not smoke, and has no recent travel.

exam_results.HEENT exam: Uvula deviated to the left with right peritonsillar swelling.

case_explanation: Muffled voice, uvular deviation, and CT findings indicate peritonsillar abscess.
full_explanation: Unilateral swelling with uvular deviation and muffled voice suggests peritonsillar abscess. CT confirms. In future cases, prioritize airway assessment and drainage.

history: A 9-year-old girl is brought in by her mother for three days of sore throat with a runny nose and cough. Her mom says she is still playing but tires more easily and has been sleeping more. Her younger brother has a cold, and several classmates were out sick last week. She has no significant past medical history and is up to date on vaccines. No vomiting, abdominal pain, or urinary symptoms.
case_explanation: Sore throat with cough, rhinorrhea, and negative strep test suggests viral pharyngitis.
full_explanation: Upper respiratory symptoms with negative strep testing suggest viral pharyngitis. Imaging is normal. In future cases, avoid unnecessary antibiotics when viral features predominate.

history: Mr. S is a 30-year-old man who returned from overseas travel with fever and a severe sore throat. He says it feels like there is a thick coating in his throat and his neck is swollen and tender. He is not up to date on childhood immunizations and has not seen a doctor in years. He denies cough or shortness of breath and has no known chronic illnesses. He does not take daily medications and smokes occasionally.

exam_results.HEENT exam: Thick gray pharyngeal pseudomembrane with bleeding when scraped.

case_explanation: Pseudomembrane with bleeding on removal suggests diphtheria.
full_explanation: Unimmunized patient with gray adherent pseudomembrane and cervical swelling suggests diphtheria. Culture confirms. In future cases, give antitoxin early and isolate.

history: Ms. A is a 26-year-old graduate student who reports a clear runny nose, sneezing, and itchy eyes that flare every spring. She notices symptoms worsen when she opens her windows or spends time in a park. She has no fever, sore throat, or body aches. She has a history of eczema, takes no daily medications, and her mother has seasonal allergies. She does not smoke and has not traveled recently.

exam_results.Nasal exam: Pale, boggy turbinates with clear discharge.

case_explanation: Seasonal rhinorrhea with itchy eyes and boggy turbinates suggests allergic rhinitis.
full_explanation: Clear rhinorrhea, sneezing, and itchy eyes with boggy turbinates indicate allergic rhinitis. Eosinophilia supports. In future cases, identify seasonal triggers.

history: A 4-year-old boy started preschool this week and now has a runny nose and mild cough for two days. His mother says he had a low-grade fever last night but is drinking fluids and playing today. He has no chronic medical problems and is up to date on vaccines. No vomiting, ear pain, or breathing difficulty. No recent travel.
case_explanation: Acute rhinorrhea with cough and normal labs suggests viral URI.
full_explanation: Short course of rhinorrhea and cough with normal exam suggests viral URI. In future cases, provide supportive care and avoid antibiotics.

history: Mr. L is a 39-year-old accountant who has felt constantly stuffed up for weeks and relies on an OTC nasal spray several times a day. He says the congestion and runny nose return quickly if he misses a dose. He has no fever or facial pain and denies allergies. He has hypertension controlled with amlodipine and takes no other daily meds. He does not smoke.
case_explanation: Chronic congestion after prolonged topical decongestant use suggests rebound rhinitis.
full_explanation: Overuse of topical decongestants causes rebound congestion and rhinorrhea. Normal imaging helps exclude sinusitis. In future cases, ask about OTC nasal spray use.

history: Ms. C is a 22-year-old woman who reports clear watery drainage from her right nostril and a dull headache after a motorcycle crash two days ago. She notices the fluid increases when she leans forward or strains. She has no fever and no focal neurologic symptoms. She has no significant past medical history and takes no daily medications. She does not use tobacco or illicit drugs.
case_explanation: Unilateral clear rhinorrhea after trauma with positive beta-2 transferrin indicates CSF leak.
full_explanation: Post-traumatic unilateral watery rhinorrhea with beta-2 transferrin confirms CSF leak. CT shows basilar skull fracture. In future cases, treat as a risk for meningitis.

history: A 51-year-old woman has nasal congestion, facial pressure, and thick yellow nasal discharge for about ten days. She felt briefly better midweek, then her symptoms worsened again. She has a history of allergies and says OTC decongestants and saline sprays have not helped. She has no dental pain or vision changes. She takes cetirizine as needed and does not smoke.
case_explanation: Purulent discharge with facial pain and CT opacification suggests bacterial sinusitis.
full_explanation: Persistent symptoms with purulent drainage and sinus tenderness suggest bacterial sinusitis. CT shows sinus opacification. In future cases, use duration and double-worsening to distinguish from viral illness.

history: Mr. H is a 59-year-old man with diabetes and hypertension who presents with crushing chest pressure for 45 minutes radiating to his left arm. He is sweaty, nauseated, and says it feels like an elephant sitting on his chest; antacids did not help. He has a strong family history of early heart disease and had similar but milder episodes with exertion in the past. He takes metformin and lisinopril. He does not smoke and has no recent illness.

imaging_results.ECG: ST elevations in leads II, III, aVF.

case_explanation: Crushing chest pain with inferior ST elevations indicates STEMI.
full_explanation: Classic ischemic chest pain with ST elevations and elevated troponin indicates STEMI. CXR helps exclude dissection. In future cases, activate reperfusion immediately.

history: Ms. W is a 68-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension who reports sudden, severe chest pain described as tearing and radiating to her back. She briefly passed out at home and feels the pain is unlike anything she has experienced. She has no recent trauma, exertion, or illness. She takes amlodipine but admits she sometimes misses doses. She does not smoke.

exam_results.Vital signs: BP 190/100 in right arm, 165/90 in left arm.

case_explanation: Tearing chest pain with pulse differential and CTA findings indicates dissection.
full_explanation: Sudden severe pain radiating to the back with BP differential suggests dissection. CTA confirms. In future cases, control blood pressure and obtain emergent imaging.

history: A 46-year-old woman on oral contraceptives develops sharp chest pain with deep breaths and shortness of breath after a long flight. She denies fever or cough and feels anxious. Her mother had a DVT in her 50s. She has no prior clots, is a nonsmoker, and takes no daily medications besides her OCP.
case_explanation: Pleuritic chest pain with risk factors and CTA findings indicates PE.
full_explanation: Pleuritic pain with tachycardia and risk factors suggests PE. Elevated D-dimer and CTA confirm. In future cases, use risk stratification to guide imaging.

history: A 29-year-old man reports sharp, pleuritic chest pain that improves when he leans forward and worsens when lying flat. He had a viral illness a week ago and now feels low-grade fevers and fatigue. He has no exertional symptoms and no cardiac history. He takes no daily medications and does not use drugs.

exam_results.Cardiac auscultation: Friction rub at left sternal border.

imaging_results.ECG: Diffuse ST elevations with PR depression.

case_explanation: Pleuritic pain relieved by leaning forward with diffuse ST elevations suggests pericarditis.
full_explanation: Positional chest pain, friction rub, and ECG changes indicate pericarditis. Echo shows small effusion. In future cases, assess for tamponade signs.

history: Ms. G is a 38-year-old woman who has burning chest discomfort after meals and at night with a sour taste in her mouth. She says antacids help and she avoids spicy foods. She denies exertional symptoms and has no cardiac history. She had reflux during pregnancy years ago and takes ibuprofen occasionally for headaches. She does not smoke.
case_explanation: Postprandial burning chest discomfort suggests reflux.
full_explanation: Chest discomfort related to meals with regurgitation suggests GERD. Normal ECG makes ischemia less likely. In future cases, assess for alarm features.

history: A 27-year-old woman describes sudden episodes of rapid heartbeat that start and stop abruptly. She says they last 10–20 minutes, sometimes with lightheadedness, and improve when she bears down or coughs. She has no chest pain and is otherwise healthy. She drinks coffee daily, takes no medications, and has no family history of sudden death. No recent illness.
case_explanation: Paroxysmal palpitations responsive to Valsalva with narrow-complex tachycardia suggest AVNRT.
full_explanation: Abrupt onset and termination with Valsalva response and narrow-complex tachycardia indicate AVNRT. Echo excludes structural disease. In future cases, ask about triggers and consider ambulatory monitoring.

history: Mr. B is a 72-year-old man who reports intermittent palpitations and fatigue for several months. He sometimes checks his pulse and says it feels irregular. He has hypertension and drinks two to three cups of coffee daily. He denies syncope or chest pain. He takes a beta-blocker and lives with his spouse.

imaging_results.ECG: Absent P waves with irregularly irregular rhythm.

case_explanation: Irregularly irregular rhythm with absent P waves suggests atrial fibrillation.
full_explanation: Palpitations with irregularly irregular rhythm and absent P waves indicate atrial fibrillation. Echo shows atrial enlargement. In future cases, assess anticoagulation need.

history: A 32-year-old woman reports palpitations, tremor, and heat intolerance for several months. She has lost weight despite increased appetite and feels restless and anxious. She notes her eyes feel gritty and says her mother had thyroid disease. She takes no daily medications and does not smoke. No recent infections.
case_explanation: Palpitations with goiter, suppressed TSH, and diffuse uptake suggest Graves disease.
full_explanation: Thyrotoxic symptoms with goiter and diffuse uptake indicate Graves disease. In future cases, check for ophthalmopathy and treat thyrotoxicosis promptly.

history: A 24-year-old woman has palpitations and episodic shortness of breath. A prior clinician told her she has a click in her heart. She has no syncope, no chest pain, and no family history of sudden death. She exercises regularly and takes no daily medications. No recent illness.

exam_results.Cardiac auscultation: Mid-systolic click with late systolic murmur.

imaging_results.Echocardiogram: Mitral valve prolapse with mild regurgitation.

case_explanation: Palpitations with mid-systolic click and echo findings suggest MVP.
full_explanation: Auscultatory findings and echo confirm MVP. Palpitations are common. In future cases, evaluate for regurgitation severity.

history: A 29-year-old man reports palpitations, anxiety, and tremor after using cocaine at a party. He feels amped up and cannot sit still, but denies chest pain. He has no prior cardiac history. He drinks alcohol on weekends and does not take daily medications. No recent illness.
case_explanation: Palpitations with stimulant use and sinus tachycardia suggests substance-induced symptoms.
full_explanation: Cocaine use with tachycardia and hypertension suggests stimulant-induced palpitations. ECG shows sinus tachycardia. In future cases, screen for stimulant use when palpitations are acute.

history: Ms. N is a 44-year-old woman who developed sudden swelling and pain in her left calf two days after a transatlantic flight. She says the leg feels tight and heavier than the other. She takes oral contraceptives and has no prior clots. No fever or trauma. She does not smoke and has no recent surgeries.

exam_results.Extremity edema exam: Unilateral left leg edema and calf tenderness.

case_explanation: Unilateral swelling after prolonged travel with positive ultrasound suggests DVT.
full_explanation: Risk factors and unilateral edema suggest DVT. Elevated D-dimer and duplex ultrasound confirm. In future cases, evaluate for PE symptoms and start anticoagulation promptly.

history: A 71-year-old man with known heart failure reports gradual worsening leg swelling and shortness of breath. He sleeps on three pillows and gets winded walking across the room. He admits he has been eating more salty takeout recently. He takes furosemide and lisinopril. No chest pain, fever, or cough.

imaging_results.Chest X-ray: Pulmonary vascular congestion and small pleural effusions.

case_explanation: Bilateral edema with dyspnea, elevated BNP, and congestion suggests heart failure.
full_explanation: Volume overload with pulmonary congestion and elevated BNP indicates heart failure exacerbation. Echo shows reduced EF. In future cases, assess volume status and adjust diuretics.

history: A 30-year-old man notices puffiness around his eyes and swelling of both ankles for two weeks. He says his urine looks foamy and he has gained a few pounds. He had a bad cold about a month ago. No fevers or flank pain. He has no known kidney disease and takes no daily meds.
case_explanation: Edema with heavy proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia suggests nephrotic syndrome.
full_explanation: Edema, proteinuria, and hypoalbuminemia indicate nephrotic syndrome. Hyperlipidemia is supportive. In future cases, quantify proteinuria and evaluate secondary causes.

history: Ms. V is a 55-year-old woman with chronic hepatitis C who reports abdominal bloating and leg swelling that has been getting worse for months. She bruises easily and feels more tired than usual. She denies chest pain or shortness of breath at rest. She drinks alcohol occasionally and takes no daily medications.
case_explanation: Leg swelling with ascites and stigmata of liver disease suggests cirrhosis.
full_explanation: Chronic liver disease signs with ascites and hypoalbuminemia indicate cirrhosis. Ultrasound confirms nodular liver. In future cases, evaluate for complications such as varices.

history: A 63-year-old woman has had chronic leg swelling that slowly worsened over months. She describes a heavy feeling and tightness in the skin. She had pelvic lymph node dissection for cervical cancer years ago. No pain, fever, or redness. She takes levothyroxine for hypothyroidism and lives alone.

exam_results.Extremity edema exam: Nonpitting edema with thickened skin and peau d'orange.

case_explanation: Nonpitting edema after lymph node dissection suggests lymphedema.
full_explanation: History of lymph node removal with nonpitting edema and skin changes indicates lymphedema. Lymphoscintigraphy supports impaired drainage. In future cases, emphasize compression and skin care.

history: A 19-year-old woman fainted while standing in a hot, crowded line at a concert. She remembers feeling nauseated, lightheaded, and sweaty beforehand, then woke up quickly on the floor. She had skipped breakfast and only had coffee that morning. She has no cardiac history, takes no medications, and denies drug use. No chest pain or palpitations before the episode.
case_explanation: Syncope with prodrome triggered by heat and standing suggests vasovagal syncope.
full_explanation: Classic prodrome with a trigger and quick recovery suggests vasovagal syncope. Normal ECG reduces cardiac causes. In future cases, ask about triggers and prodrome.

history: A 76-year-old man on diuretics fainted after standing up from bed in the morning. He reports poor oral intake after a recent stomach virus and feels dizzy when he stands. He has hypertension and takes hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril. He denies chest pain, palpitations, or seizure-like activity. No recent falls.
case_explanation: Syncope on standing with orthostatic vitals and dehydration suggests orthostatic hypotension.
full_explanation: Dehydration and diuretic use with orthostatic drop indicates orthostatic hypotension. Normal ECG lowers arrhythmia likelihood. In future cases, review volume status and medications.

history: A 64-year-old man with coronary artery disease collapsed suddenly while walking his dog. He says he blacked out without warning and felt palpitations afterward. He has a history of a prior MI and reduced ejection fraction. He takes a beta-blocker and aspirin. No recent illness or dehydration.
case_explanation: Abrupt syncope without prodrome with VT on monitoring suggests arrhythmic syncope.
full_explanation: Sudden syncope without warning in a patient with structural heart disease suggests ventricular arrhythmia. Monitoring confirms VT. In future cases, treat as high risk and consider ICD evaluation.

history: A 78-year-old woman has had episodes of lightheadedness and passed out once while walking uphill. She also reports chest tightness and shortness of breath with exertion. She has hypertension and hyperlipidemia and takes amlodipine and a statin. She denies fever, recent infection, or medication changes. No history of seizures.

exam_results.Cardiac auscultation: Harsh systolic murmur at right upper sternal border radiating to carotids.

imaging_results.Echocardiogram: Severe aortic stenosis with valve area 0.7 cm2.

case_explanation: Exertional syncope with harsh systolic murmur and echo findings indicates severe aortic stenosis.
full_explanation: Classic triad of syncope, angina, and dyspnea with a harsh murmur suggests severe AS. Echo confirms critical valve area. In future cases, refer promptly for valve intervention.

history: A 52-year-old woman recently had knee surgery and collapsed at home. She reports pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath just before she passed out. She has been mostly bedridden since surgery. She has no fever or cough and takes only postoperative pain medications. No prior clotting history.
case_explanation: Syncope with pleuritic pain and CTA findings indicates PE.
full_explanation: Post-surgical risk with syncope, hypoxia, and pleuritic pain suggests PE. CTA confirms. In future cases, assess for hemodynamic stability and treat urgently.

history: Mr. A is a 23-year-old warehouse employee who presents to the clinic with gradual onset abdominal discomfort over the past 12 hours. He describes a dull, intermittent ache that started around his belly button and has since shifted toward the lower right side. He feels mildly nauseated but has not vomited, and he skipped lunch yesterday because a busy shift ran long. He has had no diarrhea, constipation, urinary symptoms, or prior abdominal surgeries. He lives with roommates and has no recent travel.

exam_results.Abdominal exam: RLQ tenderness with rebound at McBurney point.

imaging_results.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: Enlarged appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding.

case_explanation: Migratory RLQ pain with imaging findings suggests appendicitis.
full_explanation: Classic migratory pain with RLQ tenderness and elevated WBC indicates appendicitis. CT confirms. In future cases, consider early surgical evaluation.

history: Ms. R is a 41-year-old accountant who reports episodic right upper abdominal pain that flares after greasy meals. The pain radiates to her right shoulder and lasts a few hours, and today it is worse than prior episodes. She feels nauseated but has not vomited. She has no known gallstones, no recent travel, and no change in bowel habits. She takes no daily medications.

exam_results.Abdominal exam: RUQ tenderness with positive Murphy sign.

imaging_results.RUQ Ultrasound: Gallstones, gallbladder wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid.

case_explanation: RUQ pain with fever, Murphy sign, and ultrasound findings indicates cholecystitis.
full_explanation: Postprandial RUQ pain with fever and Murphy sign suggests cholecystitis. Ultrasound confirms. In future cases, assess for complications like choledocholithiasis.

history: Mr. T is a 50-year-old restaurant manager who presents with severe upper abdominal pain that began suddenly after a weekend of heavy drinking. He describes constant, deep epigastric pain that radiates to his back and has been vomiting repeatedly. He has had poor appetite for two days and says nothing relieves the pain. He has no prior episodes of pancreatitis but does drink daily. No recent trauma or new medications.

imaging_results.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: Inflamed pancreas with peripancreatic fat stranding.

case_explanation: Epigastric pain radiating to the back with elevated lipase suggests pancreatitis.
full_explanation: Severe epigastric pain with vomiting and elevated lipase indicates pancreatitis. CT shows inflammation. In future cases, address alcohol use and assess severity.

history: Mr. D is a 66-year-old retired teacher with known diverticulosis who reports left lower abdominal pain for two days. He describes a steady, localized ache with low-grade fevers and has felt constipated. He has no vomiting, urinary symptoms, or recent antibiotic use. He notes mild loss of appetite and has not traveled recently.

imaging_results.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: Segmental colonic wall thickening with pericolonic fat stranding.

case_explanation: LLQ pain with fever and CT findings suggests diverticulitis.
full_explanation: Localized LLQ tenderness with systemic signs suggests diverticulitis. CT confirms inflammatory changes. In future cases, assess for complications like abscess.

history: Ms. K is a 27-year-old graduate student who presents with lower abdominal pain and light vaginal spotting. Her last menstrual period was about seven weeks ago. She describes intermittent cramping and feels a bit dizzy when standing. She has not yet seen an OB provider and is unsure about her pregnancy status. She has no urinary symptoms or recent illness.

lab_results.Serum hCG: Positive with level above discriminatory zone.

imaging_results.Transvaginal Ultrasound: No intrauterine pregnancy; right adnexal mass.

case_explanation: Abdominal pain with positive hCG and no intrauterine pregnancy suggests ectopic pregnancy.
full_explanation: Positive hCG with adnexal mass and absent intrauterine pregnancy indicates ectopic pregnancy. In future cases, treat urgently to prevent rupture.

history: A 34-year-old man reports burning chest discomfort after meals and at night with sour-tasting regurgitation. He says symptoms are worse when he lies down and sometimes wake him from sleep. He has no weight loss or difficulty swallowing. He has a history of seasonal allergies and takes no daily medications. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol socially.
case_explanation: Postprandial burning with erosive esophagitis indicates GERD.
full_explanation: Typical reflux symptoms with distal erosive esophagitis confirm GERD. In future cases, check for alarm features and consider PPI therapy.

history: A 52-year-old woman has gnawing epigastric burning that improves with food and returns at night. She uses NSAIDs daily for arthritis and has noticed occasional dark stools. She feels more fatigued lately but has no vomiting. She takes no anticoagulants and has no prior ulcer history.
case_explanation: Epigastric burning with H. pylori and duodenal ulcer indicates PUD.
full_explanation: Nocturnal epigastric pain with H. pylori and endoscopic ulcer confirms PUD. NSAID use is a risk factor. In future cases, treat H. pylori and reduce NSAIDs.

history: A 29-year-old woman has sudden retrosternal burning and painful swallowing after taking doxycycline without water before bed. She says it feels like the pill is stuck and has avoided eating since. She has no fever or cough. She takes no other medications and has no history of reflux.
case_explanation: Retrosternal burning and odynophagia after doxycycline suggests pill esophagitis.
full_explanation: Temporal relationship to pill ingestion without water suggests pill esophagitis. Endoscopy confirms ulcerations. In future cases, advise taking pills with water and upright posture.

history: A 21-year-old man reports chronic heartburn and intermittent food impaction. He has asthma and allergic rhinitis and says certain foods stick in his chest. He has no weight loss or GI bleeding. He takes an inhaled steroid and uses antihistamines seasonally. He does not smoke.
case_explanation: Heartburn with dysphagia, atopy, and eosinophils suggests eosinophilic esophagitis.
full_explanation: Atopic history with food impaction and ringed esophagus suggests eosinophilic esophagitis. Biopsy confirms. In future cases, consider dietary triggers and topical steroids.

history: A 60-year-old man reports long-standing heartburn and regurgitation that is worse when lying down. He also notes early satiety and a sensation of fullness after small meals. He has a history of obesity and drinks alcohol on weekends. He takes no daily medications and has no weight loss.
case_explanation: Heartburn with reflux on barium swallow suggests hiatal hernia.
full_explanation: Reflux symptoms with imaging showing herniation of stomach through diaphragm indicate hiatal hernia. In future cases, assess for complications like esophagitis.

history: A 26-year-old man has acute nausea, vomiting, and watery diarrhea after eating at a street food festival. Several friends are sick as well. He feels dehydrated, has mild cramping, and has been unable to keep down fluids. He has no chronic medical problems and takes no daily medications.

exam_results.Abdominal exam: Mild diffuse tenderness without peritoneal signs.

case_explanation: Acute vomiting and diarrhea after exposure suggests viral gastroenteritis.
full_explanation: Short, self-limited GI illness with exposure history and no focal findings suggests viral gastroenteritis. Labs show dehydration. In future cases, focus on rehydration.

history: A 63-year-old man with prior abdominal surgery has crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and bilious vomiting. He has not passed gas in 24 hours and feels bloated. He has a history of hernia repair and takes a daily aspirin. No recent travel or sick contacts.

exam_results.Abdominal exam: Distended abdomen with high-pitched bowel sounds.

imaging_results.Abdominal X-ray: Dilated small bowel with air-fluid levels.

case_explanation: Bilious vomiting with distension and air-fluid levels suggests SBO.
full_explanation: Prior surgery with obstructive symptoms and imaging showing transition point indicates SBO. In future cases, monitor for strangulation and manage with NG decompression.

history: A 24-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes presents with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain after missing insulin doses for two days. She feels very thirsty and has been urinating frequently. She has had similar episodes when she was ill. She takes insulin only and has no other chronic disease.
case_explanation: Nausea and vomiting with hyperglycemia, ketosis, and acidosis indicate DKA.
full_explanation: Missed insulin with hyperglycemia, anion gap acidosis, and ketones indicates DKA. In future cases, initiate fluids and insulin promptly.

history: A 58-year-old man reports morning headaches with nausea and projectile vomiting. He says his balance has been worsening over several weeks and he feels unsteady when walking. He has lost weight and has occasional blurred vision. He has no recent infections or head trauma.

imaging_results.MRI Brain: Posterior fossa mass with obstructive hydrocephalus.

case_explanation: Morning headaches with vomiting and papilledema suggest increased intracranial pressure.
full_explanation: Progressive headaches, papilledema, and vomiting indicate increased ICP. MRI reveals a posterior fossa mass. In future cases, treat as neurologic emergency.

history: A 22-year-old woman at 9 weeks gestation has severe nausea and vomiting and cannot keep fluids down. She has lost weight and feels dizzy when standing. She has no abdominal pain or fever. This is her first pregnancy and she takes prenatal vitamins only.
case_explanation: Severe vomiting in early pregnancy with ketonuria suggests hyperemesis gravidarum.
full_explanation: Persistent vomiting with weight loss and ketonuria in early pregnancy indicates hyperemesis. Ultrasound confirms IUP. In future cases, treat with fluids and antiemetics.

history: A 29-year-old man has profuse watery diarrhea and crampy abdominal pain for two days after camping and drinking from a stream. He also has nausea but no blood in the stool. A few friends on the trip developed similar symptoms. He takes no daily medications and has no chronic illnesses. No recent travel outside the country.
case_explanation: Watery diarrhea after stream exposure with positive stool antigen suggests giardiasis.
full_explanation: Exposure to untreated water with watery diarrhea suggests Giardia. Stool antigen confirms. In future cases, ask about travel and water sources.

history: A 33-year-old woman developed severe watery diarrhea and abdominal pain a few days after finishing clindamycin for a dental infection. She has low-grade fevers and feels dehydrated. She has no recent travel and no known inflammatory bowel disease. She takes no daily medications and lives with her partner.

imaging_results.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: Colonic wall thickening consistent with colitis.

case_explanation: Watery diarrhea after antibiotics with positive toxin PCR indicates C. difficile.
full_explanation: Recent antibiotic use with fever and watery diarrhea suggests C. difficile. PCR confirms and CT shows colitis. In future cases, avoid unnecessary antibiotics.

history: A 24-year-old man reports three months of bloody diarrhea with urgency and crampy abdominal pain. He has lost weight and feels fatigued. He also notes tender red nodules on his legs at times. He has no recent travel and no family history of colon cancer. He does not smoke.

imaging_results.Colonoscopy: Continuous mucosal inflammation starting at the rectum.

case_explanation: Bloody diarrhea with continuous colitis suggests ulcerative colitis.
full_explanation: Chronic bloody diarrhea with continuous rectal involvement indicates ulcerative colitis. Extraintestinal findings support IBD. In future cases, assess disease extent and severity.

history: A 41-year-old woman has chronic watery diarrhea and episodic flushing. She says she sometimes wheezes and feels her heart race during episodes. She has had intermittent abdominal cramps for months. She has no recent travel or antibiotic use. She takes no daily medications and does not smoke. She works as an office administrator and recently started wearing more loose clothing because of the flushing. Her father has hypertension.
case_explanation: Watery diarrhea with flushing and elevated 5-HIAA suggests carcinoid syndrome.
full_explanation: Triad of diarrhea, flushing, and wheezing suggests carcinoid syndrome. Elevated 5-HIAA and imaging confirm metastatic neuroendocrine tumor. In future cases, consider serotonin-secreting tumors with secretory diarrhea.

history: A 36-year-old woman reports bulky, foul-smelling stools, bloating, and weight loss. She has an itchy rash on her elbows that comes and goes. She says symptoms are worse after pasta or bread. She has no fevers or recent travel. She works as a schoolteacher and has been under some stress lately. Her mother has a history of autoimmune thyroid disease.

imaging_results.Upper Endoscopy: Scalloped duodenal folds with villous atrophy on biopsy.

case_explanation: Steatorrhea with dermatitis herpetiformis and positive tTG suggests celiac disease.
full_explanation: Malabsorption with dermatitis herpetiformis indicates celiac disease. Positive serology and villous atrophy confirm. In future cases, assess nutritional deficiencies.

history: A 68-year-old man on oxycodone for chronic back pain reports constipation and straining for three weeks. He feels bloated and says stools are hard and infrequent. He has no blood in stool or weight loss. He takes a stool softener only occasionally and has no history of colon cancer. No recent travel. He is retired and spends most of the day sitting while reading or watching television. His older brother has diabetes.
case_explanation: Constipation with opioid use and stool burden suggests medication-induced constipation.
full_explanation: Ongoing opioid use commonly causes constipation. Exam shows stool burden. In future cases, initiate bowel regimen with opioid therapy.

history: A 52-year-old woman has constipation, weight gain, and cold intolerance for six months. She feels sluggish and says her skin is dry. She has no abdominal pain or blood in stool. She has hyperlipidemia and takes a statin. Her sister takes medication for a thyroid condition. She works from home and has noticed she is less active than before.
case_explanation: Constipation with elevated TSH and low T4 suggests hypothyroidism.
full_explanation: Constipation with systemic hypothyroid symptoms and labs indicates hypothyroidism. In future cases, check thyroid function in chronic constipation.

history: A 61-year-old man reports progressive constipation and thinner stools with unintentional weight loss. He feels more tired than usual and has decreased appetite. He has never had a colonoscopy. He smokes one pack per day and eats a low-fiber diet. No recent travel.
case_explanation: Constipation with weight loss, anemia, and obstructing mass suggests colon cancer.
full_explanation: Alarm features with obstructing mass indicate colon cancer. Colonoscopy confirms. In future cases, prioritize colonoscopy for red flags.

history: A 34-year-old woman reports chronic constipation with bloating that improves after she has a bowel movement. She has no weight loss or bleeding and says stress makes symptoms worse. She works a desk job and eats irregular meals. She takes no daily medications and has no family history of IBD.
case_explanation: Constipation with bloating and relief after defecation suggests IBS-C.
full_explanation: Chronic constipation with bloating and symptom relief after bowel movement suggests IBS-C. Normal labs and imaging support functional disorder. In future cases, screen for alarm features.

history: A 72-year-old woman on anticholinergic medications has severe constipation and abdominal distension with confusion. Family says she has not had a bowel movement in over a week. She has Parkinson disease and takes multiple medications. No recent abdominal surgery or travel.

imaging_results.Abdominal X-ray: Massive colonic dilation consistent with pseudo-obstruction.

case_explanation: Severe constipation with colonic dilation suggests acute pseudo-obstruction.
full_explanation: Anticholinergic use with severe distension and colonic dilation indicates Ogilvie syndrome. Imaging shows pseudo-obstruction. In future cases, manage with decompression and medication review.

history: A 31-year-old woman reports bloating and abdominal discomfort after meals, often relieved by bowel movements. She alternates between constipation and diarrhea and says symptoms flare during stressful weeks. She has no weight loss or bleeding. She takes no daily medications and has no family history of colon cancer. No recent travel.
case_explanation: Bloating with symptom relief after defecation suggests IBS.
full_explanation: Meal-related bloating with bowel habit changes and normal labs suggests IBS. In future cases, assess for alarm features and dietary triggers.

history: A 40-year-old man reports bloating, flatulence, and greasy stools after a camping trip where he drank untreated water. He says his stools float and smell foul. He has no fever or blood in stool. He takes no daily medications and has no chronic illnesses. He works in landscaping and has had a few similar stomach illnesses in the past, though none this severe. His children are healthy.
case_explanation: Bloating with flatulence and positive stool antigen suggests giardiasis.
full_explanation: Exposure to untreated water with bloating and greasy stools indicates Giardia. Stool antigen confirms. In future cases, ask about travel and water sources.

history: A 58-year-old woman has bloating, chronic diarrhea, and weight loss. She underwent pancreatic surgery for cancer years ago and has had oily stools since. She feels fatigued and has difficulty maintaining weight. She takes pancreatic enzymes inconsistently. No recent travel.
case_explanation: Bloating and steatorrhea with low fecal elastase suggests pancreatic insufficiency.
full_explanation: History of pancreatic disease with low fecal elastase indicates exocrine insufficiency. Imaging shows atrophic pancreas. In future cases, consider enzyme replacement.

history: A 47-year-old woman with long-standing diabetes reports early satiety, nausea, and bloating after meals. She sometimes vomits undigested food hours after eating. She has poor glucose control and has been told she has neuropathy. She takes insulin and metformin. No fevers. She works part-time at a dental office and often eats quickly between appointments. Her father has hypertension.
case_explanation: Postprandial bloating with delayed gastric emptying suggests gastroparesis.
full_explanation: Long-standing diabetes with delayed gastric emptying indicates gastroparesis. In future cases, assess glycemic control and gastric motility.

history: A 62-year-old woman reports progressive bloating, early satiety, and pelvic pressure over three months. She has lost weight and feels fatigued. She says her clothes fit tighter around the waist. She has no change in bowel habits and no fever. She is postmenopausal. She recently retired and has been less active over the past year. Her mother had osteoporosis.
case_explanation: Bloating with adnexal mass and ascites suggests ovarian cancer.
full_explanation: Persistent bloating with early satiety and adnexal mass indicates ovarian malignancy. Elevated CA-125 and ultrasound with ascites support. In future cases, expedite gynecologic oncology referral.

history: A 27-year-old man has bright red blood on toilet paper after bowel movements with sharp pain during defecation. He has been constipated and straining. He denies weight loss or abdominal pain. He takes no daily medications and has no family history of colon cancer. He works in construction and often delays using the bathroom during the workday. He has had similar episodes during periods of constipation before.
case_explanation: Painful bright red blood with fissure on anoscopy indicates anal fissure.
full_explanation: Pain with defecation and fissure on exam indicates anal fissure. Normal CBC suggests no significant anemia. In future cases, address constipation and provide topical therapy.

history: A 52-year-old woman notices painless bright red blood in the toilet bowl. She says it happens after long days of sitting at work. She has no weight loss or abdominal pain. She has a history of constipation and takes no daily medications. No family history of colon cancer. She works in an office and often sits for most of the day. She has noticed the bleeding more after periods of straining.
case_explanation: Painless bright red blood with hemorrhoids on anoscopy suggests internal hemorrhoids.
full_explanation: Painless bleeding with hemorrhoids on anoscopy indicates internal hemorrhoids. In future cases, evaluate for anemia if bleeding is chronic.

history: A 60-year-old man reports fatigue, weight loss, and intermittent maroon stools over several months. He feels more short of breath with exertion. He has a long smoking history and has never had a colonoscopy. He denies abdominal pain. No recent travel.

imaging_results.Colonoscopy: Ulcerated mass in the descending colon.

case_explanation: Maroon stools with anemia and colon mass suggests colon cancer.
full_explanation: Chronic blood loss with anemia and colon mass indicates colon cancer. Colonoscopy confirms. In future cases, prioritize colonoscopy with red flags.

history: A 28-year-old woman has crampy abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea for two months. She also has mouth ulcers and joint aches. She has lost a few pounds and feels tired. She has no recent travel or antibiotic use. She does not smoke. She works as a graduate student and has been under significant stress recently. Her mother has seasonal allergies.

imaging_results.Colonoscopy: Patchy transmural inflammation with skip lesions.

case_explanation: Bloody diarrhea with skip lesions and extraintestinal findings suggests Crohn disease.
full_explanation: Transmural inflammation with skip lesions indicates Crohn disease. Extraintestinal manifestations support IBD. In future cases, evaluate for fistulas and strictures.

history: A 74-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation reports sudden crampy abdominal pain followed by bloody diarrhea. She feels weak and lightheaded. She takes warfarin but has missed doses recently. She has no recent travel or sick contacts. No prior GI bleeding. She lives alone and was doing housework when the pain began. Her medical history also includes hypertension.

exam_results.Abdominal exam: Tenderness out of proportion to exam.

case_explanation: Pain out of proportion with bloody diarrhea and CTA findings suggests ischemic colitis.
full_explanation: Vascular risk with sudden pain and bloody diarrhea suggests ischemic colitis. Elevated lactate and CTA confirm. In future cases, address hemodynamics and anticoagulation needs.

history: A 26-year-old man has intermittent dysphagia and food impaction. He has asthma and eczema and says certain foods stick in his chest. He has no weight loss or GI bleeding. He uses an inhaled steroid and takes antihistamines seasonally. No recent travel. He works in a call center and has had similar episodes a few times over the past year.
case_explanation: Dysphagia to solids and liquids with bird-beak narrowing suggests achalasia.
full_explanation: Progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids with manometry findings indicates achalasia. Barium swallow shows bird-beak. In future cases, consider pseudoachalasia in older patients.

history: A 68-year-old man with a smoking history reports progressive difficulty swallowing solids and weight loss. He also has painful swallowing and decreased appetite. He drinks alcohol daily and has chronic reflux symptoms. He has no recent infections. He takes no daily medications.
case_explanation: Progressive solid-food dysphagia with weight loss and mass indicates esophageal cancer.
full_explanation: Alarm features with endoscopic mass indicate esophageal cancer. CT shows local disease. In future cases, expedite endoscopy for progressive dysphagia.

history: A 26-year-old man has intermittent dysphagia and food impaction. He has asthma and eczema and says certain foods stick in his chest. He has no weight loss or GI bleeding. He uses an inhaled steroid and takes antihistamines seasonally. No recent travel.
case_explanation: Atopy with food impaction and ringed esophagus suggests eosinophilic esophagitis.
full_explanation: Allergic history with rings on endoscopy and eosinophils on biopsy indicates eosinophilic esophagitis. In future cases, consider dietary triggers and topical steroids.

history: A 30-year-old woman has sudden painful swallowing after taking ibuprofen without water before bed. She says it feels like the pill is stuck in her chest. She has no fever or cough. She takes no daily medications and has no history of reflux. She works long shifts as a nurse and often takes medications quickly between tasks. Her mother has high blood pressure.
case_explanation: Acute odynophagia after pill ingestion suggests pill esophagitis.
full_explanation: Temporal relationship to pill ingestion and mid-esophageal ulcers indicate pill esophagitis. In future cases, counsel on proper pill intake.

history: A 57-year-old man with long-standing reflux reports progressive solid-food dysphagia and regurgitation. He says he has to drink water to get food down. He has no weight loss or bleeding. He takes a daily PPI and avoids spicy foods. No recent illness. He works as a manager and says symptoms are worse after large meals in the evening.
case_explanation: Solid-food dysphagia with GERD history and endoscopic stricture suggests peptic stricture.
full_explanation: Chronic GERD with progressive solid-food dysphagia and endoscopic stricture indicates peptic stricture. In future cases, treat reflux and consider dilation.

history: A 45-year-old warehouse worker developed acute low back pain after lifting a heavy box at work. He describes a tight, aching pain across his lower back that worsens with bending and improves with rest. He has no leg weakness, numbness, or bowel/bladder changes. He has no prior back surgeries and takes ibuprofen occasionally. He does not smoke and has no recent trauma. He has had a few similar episodes over the years that improved with rest.
case_explanation: Acute pain after lifting with paraspinal tenderness suggests lumbar strain.
full_explanation: Mechanical back pain after lifting with normal neurologic exam indicates lumbar strain. Imaging rules out fracture. In future cases, look for red flags before imaging.

history: A 37-year-old woman reports low back pain radiating down the back of her left leg after a twisting injury. She describes tingling in her foot and says sitting makes it worse. She has no bowel or bladder symptoms and no fevers. She works at a desk job and takes no daily medications. No prior spine problems. She has noticed the pain is worse when she coughs or bends forward.

exam_results.Neuro exam: Positive straight leg raise on the left.

imaging_results.MRI Lumbar Spine: Left L5-S1 disk herniation impinging the S1 nerve root.

case_explanation: Radicular pain with positive straight leg raise and MRI findings suggests disk herniation.
full_explanation: Sciatica with positive straight leg raise and imaging showing disk herniation indicates radiculopathy. In future cases, monitor for neurologic deficits.

history: A 28-year-old man has chronic low back pain and morning stiffness that improves with exercise. He wakes up in the second half of the night with back pain and feels stiff for over an hour each morning. He has a history of uveitis and his father had similar back problems. He takes NSAIDs intermittently. No recent trauma or infection. He works as a graduate student and has difficulty sitting still for long periods.
case_explanation: Inflammatory back pain with HLA-B27 and sacroiliitis suggests ankylosing spondylitis.
full_explanation: Chronic inflammatory back pain with morning stiffness and sacroiliitis suggests ankylosing spondylitis. Labs support inflammation. In future cases, ask about uveitis and enthesitis.

history: A 62-year-old man with diabetes reports severe back pain with fever and difficulty walking. He says his legs feel weak and he has had trouble emptying his bladder. He has had recent skin infections. He takes metformin and insulin. He denies recent trauma. He was hospitalized earlier in the year for a foot wound that took a long time to heal.

exam_results.Neuro exam: Lower extremity weakness and decreased sensation.

imaging_results.MRI Spine: Epidural abscess compressing the thecal sac.

case_explanation: Back pain with fever and neurologic deficits suggests spinal epidural abscess.
full_explanation: Fever with back pain and neurologic deficits indicates spinal epidural abscess. MRI confirms. In future cases, treat urgently to prevent paralysis.

history: A 69-year-old man has persistent back pain, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss. He notes frequent infections and says his bones hurt, especially in his spine. He has no recent trauma. He takes no daily medications and has a family history of cancer. No bowel or bladder issues.
case_explanation: Back pain with anemia, hypercalcemia, and lytic lesions suggests multiple myeloma.
full_explanation: CRAB features with monoclonal spike and lytic lesions indicate multiple myeloma. In future cases, assess renal function and skeletal complications.

history: A 42-year-old woman has symmetric pain and swelling in her hands and wrists with morning stiffness lasting over an hour. She says opening jars has become difficult and her rings feel tight. She has no recent infections. Her mother has rheumatoid arthritis. She takes NSAIDs as needed and does not smoke. She works in accounting and has noticed symptoms are worse after periods of inactivity.

exam_results.Joint exam: Tender, swollen MCP and PIP joints bilaterally.

case_explanation: Symmetric inflammatory arthritis with positive anti-CCP suggests RA.
full_explanation: Morning stiffness with symmetric small-joint involvement and positive anti-CCP indicates RA. Erosions support diagnosis. In future cases, start DMARDs early.

history: A 66-year-old man reports chronic knee pain that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He hears grinding when he climbs stairs and says his knees feel stiff after sitting. He has a history of obesity and hypertension. He takes acetaminophen occasionally. No fevers or joint redness. He recently retired and spends more time gardening than he used to.

exam_results.Joint exam: Bony enlargement and crepitus in knees.

case_explanation: Activity-related knee pain with osteophytes indicates osteoarthritis.
full_explanation: Mechanical pain with osteophytes and normal inflammatory markers suggests osteoarthritis. In future cases, emphasize weight management and physical therapy.

history: A 58-year-old man developed sudden severe pain and swelling of his right big toe after a night of heavy food and alcohol. The joint is red and exquisitely tender. He has had similar attacks once before. He takes no daily medications and has hypertension. No recent trauma. He works in sales and says he has been eating out more often lately.
case_explanation: Acute monoarthritis with urate crystals indicates gout.
full_explanation: Classic podagra with urate crystals confirms gout. In future cases, assess for triggers and consider urate-lowering therapy.

history: A 30-year-old woman has acute knee pain and swelling with fever. She also notices a few painless skin lesions on her trunk. She has a new sexual partner and has not been using condoms. She takes no daily medications and has no history of arthritis. No recent travel. She works at a salon and noticed the joint pain developed within a few days.

exam_results.Joint exam: Large effusion with limited range of motion.
exam_results.Skin exam: Few painless pustular lesions on trunk.

case_explanation: Acute monoarthritis with pustules and positive NAAT suggests gonococcal septic arthritis.
full_explanation: Disseminated gonococcal infection causes migratory arthritis and pustular lesions. Synovial fluid and NAAT confirm. In future cases, treat promptly to prevent joint damage.

history: A 35-year-old woman reports joint pains, oral ulcers, and a rash that worsens with sun exposure. She feels fatigued and notes hair thinning. She has no recent infections. Her aunt has lupus. She takes no daily medications and does not smoke. She works in an office and has noticed symptoms flare after being outside for long periods.
case_explanation: Joint pain with malar rash and positive ANA/dsDNA suggests SLE.
full_explanation: Systemic symptoms with malar rash, oral ulcers, and positive dsDNA indicate SLE. Nonerosive arthritis is typical. In future cases, assess renal involvement.

history: A 26-year-old woman has burning urination and increased frequency for two days. She feels mild suprapubic discomfort but has no fever or flank pain. She has had one prior UTI. She is sexually active, uses condoms inconsistently, and takes no daily medications. She works as a receptionist and has been trying to drink more coffee than water during long shifts. She has no known kidney problems and says symptoms are similar to a prior episode that improved with antibiotics.
case_explanation: Dysuria with positive UA and E. coli culture indicates cystitis.
full_explanation: Typical lower UTI symptoms with UA and culture findings indicate acute cystitis. In future cases, treat promptly and consider resistance patterns.

history: A 29-year-old man has dysuria and urethral discharge after unprotected sex with a new partner. He denies fever or flank pain. He has no prior STIs and takes no daily medications. He does not smoke and drinks alcohol on weekends. He recently returned from a work trip and has had more than one new partner in the past few months. He has no history of urinary problems and has otherwise felt well.
case_explanation: Dysuria with purulent discharge and positive NAAT suggests gonorrhea.
full_explanation: Purulent discharge after unprotected sex suggests gonorrhea. NAAT confirms. In future cases, treat partners and assess for coinfections.

history: A 23-year-old woman has dysuria and urgency with pelvic discomfort. She denies fever and flank pain. She is sexually active and does not use condoms consistently. She has no prior UTIs and takes no daily medications. No recent travel. She is a nursing student and often delays urination during clinical shifts. She has noticed the discomfort is worse at the end of the day and slightly better after voiding.
case_explanation: Dysuria with sterile pyuria and positive chlamydia NAAT suggests chlamydial urethritis.
full_explanation: Sterile pyuria with dysuria and positive NAAT indicates chlamydial urethritis. In future cases, screen for coinfections and treat partners.

history: A 38-year-old woman has chronic pelvic pain and urinary urgency that worsens as her bladder fills and improves after she voids. She has had multiple negative urine cultures in the past. She works a desk job and reports high stress. She takes no daily medications and has no history of STIs. She often plans her day around restroom access and avoids long car rides because of the discomfort. She says the symptoms have slowly become more frequent over the last year.
case_explanation: Chronic dysuria with sterile urine and cystoscopic findings suggests interstitial cystitis.
full_explanation: Painful bladder syndrome with normal cultures and characteristic cystoscopy indicates interstitial cystitis. In future cases, assess for symptom triggers and pelvic floor dysfunction.

history: A 40-year-old man has burning urination and visible blood in his urine after a long bicycle ride. He has no fever and no prior UTIs. He takes no daily medications and has no history of kidney stones. He does not smoke. He has been cycling several times a week for exercise and noticed the symptoms shortly after a particularly long ride. He denies penile discharge or testicular pain.
case_explanation: Dysuria with hematuria after bicycle trauma suggests urethral injury.
full_explanation: Temporal relationship to perineal trauma with hematuria suggests urethral injury. Imaging excludes stones. In future cases, assess for urethral injury signs before catheterization.

history: A 52-year-old man reports frequent urination, excessive thirst, and blurry vision. He says he wakes up several times nightly to urinate and has gained weight. He has a family history of type 2 diabetes. He takes no daily medications and has no recent infections. He does not smoke. He works in an office, eats most meals out, and says he has felt more fatigued over the past few months.
case_explanation: Polyuria with hyperglycemia and elevated A1c suggests diabetes mellitus.
full_explanation: Osmotic diuresis from hyperglycemia causes polyuria. A1c confirms chronic diabetes. In future cases, assess complications and initiate treatment.

history: A 31-year-old woman has urinary frequency and urgency with suprapubic discomfort. She has no fever or flank pain and has had a UTI in the past. She is sexually active and uses a diaphragm for contraception. She takes no daily medications and has no recent travel. She has recently started a new relationship and says symptoms seem to appear after intercourse. She has no history of kidney stones or known structural urinary problems.
case_explanation: Frequency with positive UA indicates acute cystitis.
full_explanation: Typical lower urinary symptoms with positive UA and culture indicate cystitis. In future cases, treat based on local resistance patterns.

history: A 36-year-old woman reports intense thirst and large-volume urination for several weeks. She recently delivered a baby and had significant postpartum bleeding. She feels fatigued and has dry mouth. She takes no daily medications and has no prior endocrine disease. No recent infections. She has also noticed difficulty producing breast milk and feels unusually cold compared with others around her. She has been recovering slowly since delivery and says her energy never really returned.
case_explanation: Polyuria with high serum osmolality and low urine osmolality suggests central DI.
full_explanation: Postpartum pituitary injury can cause central DI. Hypernatremia with dilute urine confirms. In future cases, evaluate for pituitary dysfunction.

history: A 68-year-old man reports urinary frequency, weak stream, and nocturia. He says it takes a long time to start urinating and he sometimes feels he hasn't emptied completely. He has a history of hypertension and takes amlodipine. He has no dysuria or hematuria. No recent infections. He has gradually reduced his evening fluid intake because the nighttime trips to the bathroom became bothersome. His father had similar urinary symptoms in later life.
case_explanation: Lower urinary tract symptoms with enlarged smooth prostate suggests BPH.
full_explanation: Frequency, nocturia, and weak stream with enlarged prostate indicate BPH. Post-void residual supports obstruction. In future cases, assess for retention and renal effects.

history: A 58-year-old man has urinary frequency and nocturia with unintentional weight loss and bone pain. He says he feels more tired than usual. He has a long smoking history and a father who had prostate cancer. He takes no daily medications. No fever or dysuria. He has also noticed he is getting up several times a night and that the urine stream seems weaker than before. He works a physically demanding job but says the fatigue has made that harder recently.
case_explanation: LUTS with nodular prostate, high PSA, and bone mets indicates prostate cancer.
full_explanation: Obstructive symptoms with weight loss and bone pain suggest advanced prostate cancer. PSA and bone scan confirm. In future cases, evaluate metastatic symptoms with elevated PSA.

history: A 39-year-old man has sudden severe flank pain radiating to the groin with visible blood in his urine. He feels nauseated and cannot get comfortable. He has had a kidney stone once before.
