He takes no daily medications and has no fever. No recent travel. He works outdoors, sweats heavily in warm weather, and says he probably has not been drinking enough water lately. He denies any penile discharge or recent urinary symptoms before the pain started.

imaging_results.CT Abdomen/Pelvis: 3 mm right distal ureteral stone with mild hydronephrosis.

case_explanation: Colicky flank pain with hematuria and stone on CT suggests nephrolithiasis.
full_explanation: Classic renal colic with hematuria and CT-confirmed stone indicates nephrolithiasis. In future cases, assess for obstruction and infection.

history: A 67-year-old man with a long smoking history reports painless gross hematuria. He has no dysuria or flank pain. He has lost a few pounds unintentionally. He takes no daily medications and has no history of kidney stones. No recent infections. He worked around industrial chemicals earlier in life and noticed the bleeding first as occasional pink-tinged urine, which later became more obvious.
case_explanation: Painless hematuria with bladder mass suggests urothelial carcinoma.
full_explanation: Smoking-related painless hematuria with bladder lesion indicates urothelial carcinoma. Cystoscopy confirms. In future cases, evaluate hematuria urgently.

history: A 24-year-old man has cola-colored urine and periorbital swelling after a sore throat two weeks ago. He feels fatigued and his blood pressure has been higher than usual. He has no prior kidney disease. He takes no daily medications and has no recent travel. He recently recovered from an upper respiratory illness that affected several people at work. He also says his urine output has been a little lower than usual since the infection.
case_explanation: Hematuria after pharyngitis with low C3 suggests post-strep GN.
full_explanation: Nephritic syndrome following strep infection with low complement suggests PSGN. RBC casts support glomerular source. In future cases, monitor renal function and blood pressure.

history: A 29-year-old woman reports recurrent episodes of blood in her urine after viral illnesses. She feels well otherwise and has no edema. She has no family history of kidney disease. She takes no daily medications and does not smoke. No recent travel. She works with children and says the episodes often show up shortly after a cold or sore throat, then improve on their own after a few days.
case_explanation: Recurrent hematuria after infections with normal complement suggests IgA nephropathy.
full_explanation: Synpharyngitic hematuria with normal complement suggests IgA nephropathy. RBC casts indicate glomerular bleeding. In future cases, monitor proteinuria and renal function.

history: A 56-year-old man has blood in his urine and progressive hearing loss. He says several relatives had kidney disease at young ages. He has no dysuria or flank pain. He takes no daily medications and does not smoke. No recent infections. He also mentions that his vision has seemed a bit worse over time, though he has not had that checked recently. He works in a warehouse and has long assumed the hearing loss was from noise exposure.
case_explanation: Hematuria with hearing loss and family history suggests Alport syndrome.
full_explanation: Hereditary nephritis with hearing loss suggests Alport syndrome. RBC casts indicate glomerular source. In future cases, evaluate family members and monitor renal function.

history: A 19-year-old woman says her periods have been irregular since menarche. She reports acne and increased facial hair and has gained weight over the last year. She is frustrated that her cycles are unpredictable and says she struggles with oily skin. She takes no daily medications and has no known chronic diseases. Her mother has type 2 diabetes. She is a college student, has been under stress with exams, and says the symptoms have made it harder to feel confident socially.

exam_results.Skin exam: Acne and terminal hair on chin.

imaging_results.Pelvic Ultrasound: Enlarged ovaries with multiple peripheral follicles.

case_explanation: Irregular menses with hyperandrogenism and polycystic ovaries suggests PCOS.
full_explanation: Clinical hyperandrogenism with irregular cycles and polycystic ovaries indicates PCOS. In future cases, screen for metabolic complications.

history: A 28-year-old woman reports irregular periods and milky nipple discharge. She also has intermittent headaches but no visual changes. She is not pregnant and is not on birth control. She takes sertraline for anxiety and has no other medical problems. No recent travel or illness. She works in marketing and first noticed the discharge several months ago. She says the headaches are mild, come and go, and usually improve with rest.
case_explanation: Irregular menses with galactorrhea and elevated prolactin suggests prolactinoma.
full_explanation: Hyperprolactinemia with galactorrhea and MRI microadenoma indicates prolactinoma. In future cases, review medications that elevate prolactin.

history: A 45-year-old woman says her cycles have become irregular over the last year. She has hot flashes, night sweats, and poor sleep. She wonders if she is starting menopause. She has no thyroid disease and takes no daily medications. She does not smoke and has no recent stressors. She works full-time in an office and has noticed mood swings and vaginal dryness over the past several months.
case_explanation: Irregular cycles with vasomotor symptoms and elevated FSH suggest perimenopause.
full_explanation: Age-appropriate irregularity with hot flashes and elevated FSH indicates perimenopause. In future cases, counsel on symptom management and contraception.

history: A 17-year-old competitive runner reports missing her periods for several months. She has lost weight during training and says she feels cold and tired. She denies sexual activity and has no chronic medical problems. She eats irregularly during busy training weeks. No recent illness. She has increased her mileage recently and is trying to qualify for a major meet.
case_explanation: Amenorrhea with low gonadotropins and low BMI suggests hypothalamic amenorrhea.
full_explanation: Energy deficiency with low gonadotropins indicates functional hypothalamic amenorrhea. In future cases, assess nutrition and stress.

history: A 33-year-old woman reports heavy, irregular periods and easy bruising. She says her mother has a bleeding disorder and she has always bruised easily. She feels fatigued and has been told she is anemic. She takes no daily medications and has no recent surgeries. No pelvic pain. She also notices prolonged bleeding after minor cuts and often has to use extra menstrual products during her period.
case_explanation: Heavy irregular menses with prolonged aPTT and low vWF suggests vWD.
full_explanation: Mucosal bleeding with family history and low vWF indicates von Willebrand disease. In future cases, evaluate bleeding disorders in heavy menses.

history: A 24-year-old woman has sudden severe pelvic pain with nausea. She says it started abruptly while she was exercising. She has a known ovarian cyst and had a similar but milder episode in the past. She has no fever or urinary symptoms. She takes no daily medications. She was doing a high-intensity workout at the gym when the pain began and had to stop immediately.

imaging_results.Transvaginal Ultrasound with Doppler: Enlarged ovary with decreased blood flow.

case_explanation: Sudden pelvic pain with decreased ovarian blood flow suggests torsion.
full_explanation: Acute severe pain with Doppler evidence of decreased flow indicates ovarian torsion. In future cases, treat as surgical emergency.

history: A 27-year-old woman reports lower abdominal pain, fever, and vaginal discharge. She has a new sexual partner and says the pain worsens during intercourse. She has no recent travel or prior PID. She takes no daily medications and does not use condoms consistently. She works in retail and says the symptoms started a few days after a recent weekend trip.

exam_results.Pelvic exam: Cervical motion tenderness and adnexal tenderness.

imaging_results.Transvaginal Ultrasound: Thickened fallopian tubes with free pelvic fluid.

case_explanation: Pelvic pain with CMT, fever, and positive NAAT suggests PID.
full_explanation: Cervical motion tenderness with fever and STI indicates PID. Ultrasound shows tubo-ovarian inflammation. In future cases, treat promptly to prevent infertility.

history: A 32-year-old woman has chronic pelvic pain that worsens during her periods and with intercourse. She has been trying to conceive for over a year. She has no fever or urinary symptoms. Her mother had endometriosis. She takes ibuprofen as needed. She also reports pain with bowel movements around her menstrual periods and says the symptoms have slowly worsened over time.
case_explanation: Cyclic pelvic pain with dyspareunia and nodularity suggests endometriosis.
full_explanation: Cyclic pain and dyspareunia with nodularity suggest endometriosis. Ultrasound shows endometrioma. In future cases, consider laparoscopy for definitive diagnosis.

history: A 38-year-old woman reports pelvic pressure and heavy menstrual bleeding. She says her abdomen feels full and she has to urinate more often. She has a history of iron deficiency anemia and takes iron supplements. She has no fever or weight loss. No prior surgeries. She has been changing pads more frequently during her periods and feels more tired than usual at work.
case_explanation: Pelvic pressure with enlarged uterus and fibroids on ultrasound suggests fibroids.
full_explanation: Heavy bleeding and pressure with enlarged irregular uterus indicate fibroids. Ultrasound confirms. In future cases, assess impact on fertility and anemia.

history: A 29-year-old woman has pelvic pain and light spotting about six weeks after her last period. She feels dizzy and has not yet seen a prenatal provider. She has no urinary symptoms or recent illness. She takes no daily medications and is unsure of her pregnancy status. She recently stopped using contraception and thought her period was just late until the pain began.

imaging_results.Transvaginal Ultrasound: No intrauterine pregnancy; left adnexal mass.

case_explanation: Pelvic pain with positive hCG and no IUP suggests ectopic pregnancy.
full_explanation: Positive hCG with adnexal mass and absent IUP indicates ectopic pregnancy. In future cases, treat urgently to prevent rupture.

history: A 58-year-old man with long-standing diabetes reports burning and numbness in both feet, worse at night. He says socks feel too tight and he sometimes cannot feel the floor. He has poor glucose control and takes insulin and metformin. He has no back pain or recent injuries. No alcohol misuse. He works a desk job and says the numbness has made walking in the dark more difficult.

exam_results.Neuro exam: Decreased vibration and pinprick in stocking distribution.

case_explanation: Stocking-glove paresthesias with poor glycemic control suggests diabetic neuropathy.
full_explanation: Chronic hyperglycemia with distal symmetric neuropathy and abnormal NCS indicates diabetic neuropathy. In future cases, optimize glycemic control and foot care.

history: A 46-year-old woman has numbness and tingling in her hands and feet with difficulty walking. She follows a strict vegan diet and feels fatigued. She has no history of diabetes or thyroid disease. She takes a multivitamin inconsistently and has no recent infections. No alcohol use. She also reports a sore tongue and occasional trouble with balance when turning quickly.

exam_results.Neuro exam: Loss of vibration and proprioception, positive Romberg.

case_explanation: Paresthesias with macrocytic anemia and low B12 suggest deficiency.
full_explanation: Vegan diet with macrocytic anemia and posterior column findings indicates B12 deficiency. In future cases, replace B12 and assess malabsorption.

history: A 29-year-old woman reports episodic numbness in her right arm and blurred vision in her left eye that resolves over days. She feels fatigued between episodes. She has no recent infections and no history of migraines. She takes no daily medications and does not smoke. Her mother has autoimmune disease. She says the symptoms come and go unpredictably and are often followed by a period of feeling completely normal.

exam_results.Eye exam: Afferent pupillary defect on the left.

case_explanation: Disseminated neurologic symptoms with demyelinating plaques suggest MS.
full_explanation: Relapsing neurologic symptoms with optic neuritis and periventricular plaques indicate MS. Oligoclonal bands support. In future cases, assess dissemination in time and space.

history: A 35-year-old woman has numbness and tingling in the first three fingers of her right hand, worse at night and with typing. She drops objects more frequently and says shaking her hand helps. She works as a graphic designer and uses a computer all day. She takes no daily medications. No neck pain. Symptoms have gradually progressed over several months and are worse after long workdays.

exam_results.Neuro exam: Positive Tinel and Phalen at wrist.

imaging_results.Nerve conduction study: Median nerve conduction delay at wrist.

case_explanation: Median nerve distribution paresthesia with positive Phalen suggests carpal tunnel.
full_explanation: Nocturnal hand paresthesia with median nerve distribution and NCS delay indicates carpal tunnel syndrome. In future cases, consider splinting and ergonomic changes.

history: A 41-year-old man has perioral numbness and tingling in his hands with muscle cramps after thyroid surgery. He says his hands lock up at times. He takes calcium intermittently but has missed doses. He has no prior neurologic disease and no recent infections. No substance use. He also mentions muscle twitching near his mouth and has had trouble sleeping because of the cramps.
case_explanation: Perioral numbness with low calcium and recent thyroid surgery suggests hypoparathyroidism.
full_explanation: Post-thyroidectomy hypocalcemia causes paresthesias and tetany. Low calcium and prolonged QT confirm. In future cases, monitor calcium after neck surgery.
